questions.title: Longest Ocean Coastline
questions.prompt: Name the US states with the longest ocean/tidal coastline, excluding Great Lakes shoreline.
questions.disclaimer: Uses NOAA's 'general coastline' figures (straight-line, excludes bays and river tidal reaches). Great Lakes shorelines excluded — this ranks ocean/tidal coastline only. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).

questions.title: States Bordering Canada
questions.prompt: Name the US states that share a land or water border with Canada.
questions.disclaimer: Includes states with a shared land or river border with Canada, ordered by length of shared border in miles. States whose only Canadian boundary is a Great Lake shoreline are excluded. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).

source.name: US Census Bureau — State boundary data / International Boundary Commission

questions.title: States Bordering Mexico
questions.prompt: Name the US states that share a land border with Mexico.
questions.disclaimer: Only 4 states share a land border with Mexico. Ordered by length of shared border. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).

questions.title: Largest Landlocked States
questions.prompt: Name the largest landlocked US states by total area (states with no ocean coastline and no Great Lakes shoreline).
questions.disclaimer: 'Landlocked' here means no ocean coast and no Great Lakes shoreline. States along the Mississippi or other inland rivers still qualify. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: US Census Bureau — State Area Measurements

questions.title: States on the Mississippi River
questions.prompt: Name the US states whose borders are directly touched or crossed by the main stem of the Mississippi River.
questions.disclaimer: The Mississippi's main stem forms all or part of the border of, or flows through, exactly 10 states. Ordered north to south. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).

source.name: Wikipedia — Mississippi River (states bordered section, sourced from USGS)

questions.title: States Crossed by the Continental Divide
questions.prompt: Name the US states through which the Great (Continental) Divide of the Americas runs.
questions.disclaimer: The Continental Divide separates Pacific-draining watersheds from Atlantic/Gulf-draining watersheds. In the US, it runs through five contiguous states plus Alaska. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).

source.name: USGS — Continental Divide of the Americas

questions.title: States Crossed by the Appalachian Trail
questions.prompt: Name the US states the Appalachian National Scenic Trail passes through.
questions.disclaimer: The AT passes through 14 states between Springer Mountain (GA) and Mount Katahdin (ME). Ordered south to north. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).

questions.title: States Crossed by the Pacific Crest Trail
questions.prompt: Name the US states the Pacific Crest National Scenic Trail passes through.
questions.disclaimer: The PCT crosses only three states between the Mexican and Canadian borders. Ordered south to north. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).

questions.title: Most Interstate Highway Mileage
questions.prompt: Name the US states with the most miles of Interstate Highway System within their borders.
questions.disclaimer: Counts centerline miles of designated Interstate routes only (not other freeways). Ordered longest to shortest. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: Federal Highway Administration — Highway Statistics, Table HM-20

questions.title: Most Public-Use Airports
questions.prompt: Name the US states with the most public-use airports.
questions.disclaimer: Counts public-use airports (public and private-owned but open to the public) as tallied by the FAA. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: FAA — National Plan of Integrated Airport Systems (NPIAS)

questions.title: Most Bridges (by Count)
questions.prompt: Name the US states with the greatest number of bridges (highway bridges of all sizes).
questions.disclaimer: Counts entries in the National Bridge Inventory (spans of at least 20 feet on public roads). Includes both state-owned and locally-owned bridges. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: Federal Highway Administration — National Bridge Inventory

questions.title: Most Named Mountain Peaks
questions.prompt: Name the US states with the most named mountain peaks catalogued in the USGS Geographic Names Information System (GNIS).
questions.disclaimer: Counts of GNIS features with feature class 'Summit' by state. Every named summit is counted regardless of elevation. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: USGS Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) — feature class 'Summit'

questions.title: Most Named Peaks Over 5,000 ft
questions.prompt: Name the US states with the most named summits above 5,000 feet in elevation.
questions.disclaimer: Named summits above 5,000 ft (1,524 m) with recognized names in Peakbagger's state databases. Elevation cutoff is fixed, not prominence-adjusted. DC not included (source omits it).

questions.title: Largest Tribal Land Area
questions.prompt: Name the US states with the largest total area of federally recognized tribal (reservation and trust) lands.
questions.disclaimer: Total land area of federally recognized American Indian reservations plus off-reservation trust lands within each state's boundaries. DC not included (source omits it).

source.name: US Bureau of Indian Affairs / US Census Bureau — American Indian Areas

questions.title: Largest Reservoir Storage Capacity
questions.prompt: Name the US states with the largest total surface-water reservoir storage capacity.
questions.disclaimer: Sum of maximum normal storage across all dams in each state as recorded in the National Inventory of Dams. Interstate reservoirs are credited to the state hosting the dam. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: US Army Corps of Engineers — National Inventory of Dams (NID)

questions.title: Most Named Waterfalls
questions.prompt: Name the US states with the most named waterfalls catalogued in the USGS Geographic Names Information System.
questions.disclaimer: Counts of GNIS features classified as 'Falls' by state. Includes all named cascades regardless of drop height. DC not included (source omits it).

source.name: USGS Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) — feature class 'Falls'
